name: str_like
title: Detect a pattern the way SQL LIKE does

origin.description: Match the whole string the way SQL LIKE does. _ matches one character, % matches any number of characters, and a backslash escapes those two. str_like is case sensitive.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A character vector of SQL LIKE patterns. A stringr modifier is an error. % and _ inside brackets, and a backslash before either character, stay literal.

arguments.name: ignore_case
arguments.text: Deprecated in stringr 1.6.0. Supplying it warns. TRUE forwards to str_ilike. FALSE keeps the case-sensitive match. The default is the deprecated sentinel, which means the argument was not supplied.

origin.details: Before stringr 1.6.0, str_like was incorrectly case-insensitive. The pattern is rewritten to an anchored regular expression: % becomes .*, _ becomes ., and the result is wrapped with ^ and $. A missing pattern is pasted as the letters NA, so the expression is ^NA$. The match itself is stri_detect_regex with case sensitivity left on.
origin.value: A logical vector the same length as string and pattern.
origin.example:
fruit <- c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple")
result <- str_like(fruit, "app%")
writeLines(paste0('str_like(c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"), "app%") returns ', paste(result, collapse = ", "), '.'))

translation.description: Match the whole string the way SQL LIKE does. The match is case sensitive.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, stringi._na.NA, or a list of those. A list may carry names.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A plain string or list of SQL LIKE patterns. A Pattern from fixed, coll, regex, or boundary is rejected with cli_abort.

arguments.name: ignore_case
arguments.text: Defaults to lifecycle.deprecated(). If lifecycle.is_present is true, lifecycle.deprecate_warn runs. True then calls str_ilike.

translation.details: like_to_regex uses stri_replace_all_regex for the percent and underscore rules, then anchors the expression. A missing pattern becomes the letters NA inside ^ and $, because paste0 does that. The anchored text is passed through regex(ignore_case=False) and stri_detect_regex. Lengths are checked before the character check, so a size mismatch is a RecycleError.
translation.value: A list of bools. A missing result is NA.
translation.example:
from stringr.detect import str_like
fruit = ["apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"]
result = str_like(fruit, "app%")
words = ", ".join("TRUE" if item else "FALSE" for item in result)
print('str_like(c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"), "app%") returns ' + words + '.')
